feature: Pinned guides catch what you draw
summary: A guide you pin onto the picture now catches the ends of the things you draw as well as the boxes you drag: an arrow's tip, a line's end, a caliper's foot and a caption you click down all land on it, with the same yellow line and the same Command to get away from it.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. The grid flag is on by default. Open any picture, switch the grid on with View ▸ Show Grid, then press Adjust Grid on the tool bar to pin a guide or two.

try.do: Switch the grid on: View ▸ Show Grid.
Press Adjust Grid, click one line down the picture and one across it to pin two guides, then press Done.
Switch the grid off again with View ▸ Show Grid, so the guides are the only lines left.
Press A for the arrow tool and drag an arrow that ends a few points short of the vertical guide.
Press I for Measure and click two feet, putting the second one a few points short of the same guide.
Press T and click a caption down a few points short of the guide.
Draw one more arrow at the guide with Command held, and watch it stay exactly where you let go.

evaluate: When a tip catches a guide, can you tell the catch happened, or does the brighter yellow read as the same line you pinned?
Is the reach right for drawing? A guide grabs from about eight points away, the same as a dragged box.
A caption clicked near a guide now lines its left edge up on it. Is that welcome, or does a click feel like it should land exactly where you clicked?
Drawing an arrow along a guide makes it come out lying exactly on the guide. Does that feel like help or like interference?
With the grid switched off and only guides pinned, is it clear why the drawing still jumps?
rough: An arrow catches a guide whichever way it points, unlike a border found in the picture, which a level arrow can only catch down the way it is pointing. That is what lets you draw an arrow that lies exactly along a guide, and the price is that a slightly sloping arrow whose tip passes near a guide takes it and slopes a few points more. Command is the way out.

The caliper's number (the head) still lines up only with the other numbers on the canvas, not with pinned guides. It is a label rather than a measured point, so a guide has nothing to say about where it parks.

A caliper's measuring line is levelled after both feet are placed, so a horizontal caliper can catch a vertical guide and not a horizontal one. That is how the caliper has always worked, not something this changed.
The rubber band of the selection tools still does not catch a guide. It never caught the grid either, so it was left alone.
Screen Recording was granted, so the two pictures are real captures of the window, one taken with the arrow still under the button.
